## Triage order: hotspot files by blast radius

Sorting by what actually ripples — fan-in count and blast_radius_importers — not just severity.

### Refactor first

**1. `src/plugin.ts`** — fan-in 10 (p99 tier), 29 importers, blast_radius 0.58
The highest-connectivity *domain* file. Contains `buildFinished` (103 lines, 1.7x threshold). Every change here touches 29 downstream files. Split the plugin interface from the build-lifecycle logic to shrink the coupling surface.

**2. `src/utils.ts`** — fan-in 18 (!), 29 importers, blast_radius 0.58, 425-line God File
Highest fan-in in the entire repo — nearly 2x the p99 cutoff of 10. Also flagged as a large file (1.4x threshold) and carries 7 sync I/O calls. The classic "utils grab bag" that everything depends on. Split along responsibility boundaries (file ops, path helpers, config normalization) so consumers can import narrowly.

**3. `src/index.ts`** — fan-out 17 (far above p99 of 11), 460-line God File
Five God Functions stacked in one file: `build` (293 lines, 4.9x), `mainTasks` (194 lines), `normalizeOptions` (96 lines), `startWatcher` (79 lines), `buildAll` (75 lines). Fan-out 17 means it pulls in nearly everything. Fan-in is only 4 (7 importers), so while it's internally a mess, its blast radius is moderate. Refactoring here primarily makes the file editable without accidentally touching unrelated orchestration.

### Worth doing, lower priority

**4. `src/esbuild/index.ts`** — fan-out 11 (p99 tier), fan-in 1, 7 importers
Contains `runEsbuild` at 237 lines (4.0x). High fan-out means it's the build pipeline's dependency hub, but fan-in is just 1 — changes here don't propagate outward much. Extract the 38-property options bag and the function body into helpers. Improves maintainability but doesn't reduce blast radius for the rest of the graph.

### Leave alone

**`src/log.ts`** — fan-in 9 (p95), 30 importers, blast_radius 0.60
Looks scary on paper (highest importer count in the repo at 30), but fan-out is 0 and it's a logging utility. High fan-in is *correct* for infrastructure like this. Refactoring it creates churn across 30 files for no structural gain.

**`test/utils.ts`** — fan-in 9, 9 importers
Test helper. High fan-in is expected and healthy — every test file sharing a harness is the point.

**`docs/README.md`** — 679 lines, 0 importers, blast_radius 0
Big markdown file with zero code coupling. Splitting it is a docs task, not a refactoring priority.

**`src/rollup.ts`** — fan-out 7, fan-in 0, 0 importers
Nobody imports it. The `getRollupConfig` God Function (122 lines) is messy but contained — no downstream ripple.

**`src/api-extractor.ts`** — fan-out 6 (p95), fan-in 1
Minimal connectivity. The fan-out just reflects that it needs several utilities to do its job.

### Summary

| Priority | File | Fan-in | Importers | Why |
|----------|------|--------|-----------|-----|
| 1 | `src/plugin.ts` | 10 | 29 | Highest-connectivity domain file; God Function inside |
| 2 | `src/utils.ts` | 18 | 29 | 2x the p99 fan-in; grab-bag coupling everything depends on |
| 3 | `src/index.ts` | 4 (out: 17) | 7 | Five God Functions, highest fan-out; internal mess |
| 4 | `src/esbuild/index.ts` | 1 (out: 11) | 7 | High fan-out but contained; maintainability win |
| Skip | `src/log.ts` | 9 | 30 | Infrastructure; high fan-in is correct |
| Skip | `test/utils.ts` | 9 | 9 | Test harness; expected pattern |
| Skip | `docs/README.md` | 0 | 0 | No code coupling |
| Skip | `src/rollup.ts` | 0 | 0 | No downstream consumers |

The first two files account for 58 importers between them. Splitting those two would meaningfully shrink the blast radius of any future change in this codebase.
